objective: Correct a false physicality assumption in the newly added registry-to-Unity material guard: on Unity Standard materials with an active metallic/smoothness map, _GlossMapScale is a control multiplier rather than the final roughness, and the metallic/smoothness texture channels must be evaluated before comparing the actual material response inputs to the authored physical ranges.

changes.summary: Replaced scalar-only mapped-material evaluation with a fail-closed Standard-shader path that reads active _MetallicGlossMap red-channel extrema for metallic and the selected metallic/albedo alpha extrema multiplied by _GlossMapScale for smoothness, converts that smoothness interval to roughness, and requires the full effective range to remain inside the authored registry range. Source-channel decoding is cached by AssetDatabase dependency hash plus file size/time so repeated formal pre-cull checks do not repeatedly decode unchanged maps. The report now records min/max effective metallic and roughness plus their source semantics.

Raised the contract to schema 1.1 and made texture-aware metallic/roughness evaluation, Standard map-channel semantics, source-channel inspectability, full-range containment, and dependency-hash caching mandatory. Unsupported mapped texture formats remain fail-closed rather than silently reverting to misleading scalar checks.

findings: The generated PBR library writes MetallicSmoothness PNGs with metallic in R and smoothness in A, enables _METALLICGLOSSMAP and sets _GlossMapScale=1.

The previous guard treated mapped roughness as 1-_GlossMapScale. For PBR_DanchiConcrete this evaluates to 0 even though the texture actually encodes a roughness field around 0.82-0.94; that would incorrectly block the first Runner rather than detect material drift.

PBR_DanchiConcrete uses profile roughness 0.88 with +/-0.06 height-driven variation before 8-bit smoothness encoding, giving an intended roughness envelope of approximately 0.82-0.94, which is consistent with the registry range 0.78-0.94 before source quantization tolerance.

Unity Standard metallic workflow documentation states that a metallic texture uses red for metallic and alpha for smoothness, with smoothness optionally sourced from albedo alpha; the new QA follows those semantics only when the active shader is exactly Standard.

selfAudit: Mapped Standard metallic evaluation is source-channel based only when _METALLICGLOSSMAP is actually enabled; an assigned but inactive map falls back to the scalar path and is reported as such.
Mapped Standard roughness honors _SmoothnessTextureChannel: metallic-map alpha is the default source and albedo alpha is used when the material selects it.
The mapped roughness comparison uses the entire decoded alpha extrema interval after _GlossMapScale, not a midpoint, so a small physically impossible patch cannot be hidden by an acceptable average.
Mapped non-Standard shaders are rejected because their channel semantics cannot be inferred safely from Standard conventions.
PNG/JPG/JPEG source decoding is intentionally fail-closed. Adding another texture container requires an explicit reviewable decoder path rather than silently claiming its values are known.

knownLimitations: Source/GitHub inspection cannot prove the revised C# compiles under Unity 6000.3.0f1; the missing Runner remains the blocker.

Source-image channel extrema do not include GPU compression, mip filtering, anisotropic filtering, derivative behavior or final BRDF/Fresnel appearance; sealed native-4K grazing-light pixels remain authoritative.

This run does not yet force the registry physicality guard to execute before realtime ReflectionProbe.RenderProbe; formal MainCamera pre-cull remains fail-closed, and the reflection render-state fingerprint still prevents state drift, but pre-probe physicality validation is a useful next source-side integration if no Runner appears first.
A passing numeric range check cannot clear impossible_material_physics or baked_or_painted_highlights without direct review of the canonical rendered grazing crops.

implementationReadiness.reasonNoIncrease: The run fixes a correctness defect in source-side material validation but the remaining 7 readiness points stay reserved for actual Unity 6000.3.0f1 compile/runtime verification.

expectedScoreImpactAfterRealRender: Material/PBR physical plausibility: prevents texture-driven metallic or smoothness fields from escaping the authored physical ranges while also avoiding a false failure caused by misreading _GlossMapScale as final roughness.
Texture/microdetail fidelity: validates the material map channel field as a full range rather than ignoring its variation; actual texel quality and repetition still require rendered evidence.

Critical impossible_material_physics: reduces source/runtime risk from mapped metallic/smoothness values that are physically outside the declared material family, but cannot clear the critical defect without actual pixels.
Cinematic and lighting categories receive no direct points; final angular response, highlights and reflections remain render-only evidence.

nextBlocker: Unity 6000.3.0f1 Runner/Editor compile and runtime. When available, stop speculative expansion and first run the registered material physicality contract against the generated PBR scene. Confirm PBR_DanchiConcrete reports source-driven metallic 0 and roughness approximately 0.82-0.94 rather than scalar roughness 0, then execute Prepare Complete Native 4K Review Packet and score only sealed 3840x2160 hero/oblique/grazing pixels and 100% crops. If no Runner appears first, the next safe integration is to invoke this physicality guard before realtime reflection probe requests so an invalid material state never enters the cubemap baseline.
